correctness.rationale: Exact frame moments follow entrywise from the Gram matrix; a nodal polynomial forces the coefficient of z^4 to vanish under all degree-four Laurent constraints. Reduction of primitive 2p-th roots to -1 modulo p gives explicit complete parity tables excluding at most six nodes for p=7 and at most seven for p>=11. The eight-node positive construction has strict analytic weight inequalities and exact even/odd cosine moments; Chebyshev polynomials supply modes one to four, and Fourier inversion/subgroup rules handle p=3,5,7. Supplementary rational and finite-prime checker tests passed; the infinite theorem relies on the proof rather than enumeration.

value.rationale: The precise resource is the number of distinct frequency samples needed for a tight positive frame on a fixed five-site cyclic Fourier aperture. A complete prime-by-prime minimum, novel uniform eight-node design for every large twice-prime order, and a symmetric-sum obstruction for the sharp lower bound are motivated structural results beyond rank-based or finite numerical examples. They also distinguish four-site and prime-order analogues; no broader stability claim is made.
